title: LoRa Vehicle Controller: Reconstruction and Platform Redesign
summary: An STM32 and LoRa vehicle-controller project with reconstructed KiCad hardware, annotated schematics, a searchable engineering workspace, assembly evidence and a reproducible V1 firmware build. V2 hardware and a voice/text/location handheld remain under development.

validated_results.claim: Fifteen annotated schematic pages were visually inspected after export.
Presentation edits preserved all baseline components and 533 electrical pins without changing net names, values or footprints.
Two V1 builds on the recorded host and toolchain produced identical ELF, HEX and BIN hashes.
Purchasing and assembly exports reconcile physical references and separate candidate parts from holds and board features.
Viewer desktop/mobile interaction checks and 203 local HTTP links passed at the recorded checkpoint.
Eighteen quality-tool acceptance tests passed; isolated schematic generation preserved PCB, project and BOM artifacts.
Separate V2 Stage A diagnostic builds twice with identical ELF/HEX/BIN; 1328-byte BIN, nine pin-contract tests pass. No hardware operation is claimed.
Localized ground repair reduces V2 unconnected PCB items from three to zero with zero ordinary DRC errors and unchanged warnings/parity; all footprints and pad assignments preserved.

An isolated IMU interface schematic adds a 1.8 V rail and I2C/interrupt translation. Native comparison verifies exactly five changed existing connections, 356 preserved memberships and no new ERC findings; PCB integration remains pending.

An isolated mechanical study preserves all original PCB objects and fits the IMU courtyard envelopes. Native DRC exposes 136 errors across the proposed placement, blocking integration on untouched copper.

IMU2 adds a 100 pF translator bias filter with exactly two new pin memberships and all 398 preceding memberships preserved. Native ERC retains only the previous warning; no PCB integration is claimed.

Analytical load and cutoff-tolerance models expose the low-input feed conflict; proposed package-specific pin maps independently reviewed. Browser calculator parity is recorded separately from hardware qualification.
INPUT-A1 isolated schematic replaces the old input protection cell with a series-diode boundary, preserving all 344 outside-boundary memberships and adding no ERC findings.
Manufacturer review identifies a zero-reverse-voltage constraint on INPUT-A1 C1; tested analytical cases keep diode-only calculations separate from full-circuit and ADC acceptance.

BUCK33-A1 native comparison verifies the complete first 3.3 V converter replacement: 113 parts, 361 pins, all 330 outside-boundary pins preserved and no new ERC findings. Analytical and package checks do not establish hardware acceptance.

BUCK5-A1 native comparison preserves all 339 outside-boundary pins and the first converter. The 5 V candidate has 119 components and 398 pins and no new ERC findings; analytical feed limits and diode package holds remain separate from hardware acceptance.

ACT-01 verifies four buffer/bypass rail moves, exact SMC diode identities, master DNP holds, 380 outside pins and both converter sources preserved. 31 contract/population tests pass; live board and physical acceptance remain unchanged.

ACT-02 independently checks TXU0102 physical pins, new PC4 enable and pulldown, preserving 383 outside-boundary pins, both converters and ACT-01 source populations. 41 mutation tests pass; native ERC adds no findings. Live board/firmware/ordering remain unchanged.

ACT-03 independently checks ACT-02 connector/net/PG no-connect evidence and tests an executable fault-latched rearm proposal, including exact-deadline and stale-strobe counterexamples. No native circuit or hardware acceptance is inferred.

ACT-04 native candidate: 128 components, 429 pins; exactly two old memberships change and 396 are preserved; ERC zero errors and the original AD0 warning. Boolean and package evidence have separate limits.
ACT-05 tests conditional assertion/recovery arithmetic and an illustrative RC edge; fixed-window selection remains held.
ACT-06 compares five released integrated-window identities and concrete adjustable dividers with 19 numerical/rejection tests; timing and hardware remain held.
ACT-07 verifies conditional comparator/reference threshold and waveform budgets with ten numerical/rejection tests; no component or arbitrary-ramp qualification follows.
ACT-08 verifies conditional reference load, feed-floor discharge and input resistor limits with ten analytical/rejection tests; partial-power behavior remains unqualified.
ACT-09 reproduces conditional same-rail deadlines, finite hold-up and fault/restart request traces. The physical permission boundary remains unimplemented.

ACT-10 checks an exact series-switch proposal and conditional OE decay. The optimistic total capacitance ceiling is9.805pF; source timing and arbitrary brownout isolation remain unqualified. No native delta.

ACT-11 preserves 298 prior-file hashes and checks exact translator supply memberships. Eight tests verify conditional discharge arithmetic, fixed illustration inputs and rejection of unsupported acceptance claims. Typical shutdown estimates are not timing guarantees; power-only cycling retains the separate READY latch.

ACT-12 checks 30 captured pin memberships and the inherited 400 ns allocation. Nine tests cover topology drift, conditional arithmetic and missing-evidence rejection. The interactive explorer distinguishes five fault cases; receiver thresholds, pulse/loss behavior and stop response remain unqualified.

VSERVO-01 amends only isolated C11 identity and lands while preserving 429 pin memberships, 127 other full component records, both converters and ACT-01 population bytes. Native KiCad 9.0.7 reports zero ERC errors and one unchanged AD0 warning. Thirteen candidate tests, twelve conditional-model tests and 343 preserved inputs support review; reservoir, assembly and hardware acceptance remain open.

VSERVO-02 preserves 427 captured inputs and checks conditional threshold/response windows, finite event storage and recurring dissipation. Upstream energy return, reverse voltage and receiver/source limits remain unqualified. A local dissipative shunt is a next-study proposal only; VSERVO-01 stays native and no part, circuit or application is released.

POWER-DOC-01 improves native Power sheet layout and annotations without changing the VSERVO-01 electrical candidate. Captured comparison preserves 128 component records, 429 physical pin memberships and node attributes, 121 complete nets and 11 sheet identities. Thirty-seven of 38 source files, both converters, symbol definitions and population bytes are preserved. Three native commands export 11 SVG sheets; ERC has zero errors and the unchanged AD0 warning. Seventeen equivalence tests pass. Live CAD/copper and hardware release remain unchanged.

VSERVO-03 preserves 532 captured inputs, checks 14 captured power-path pin memberships and passes 16 conditional-model tests for the proposed independent switched-resistor shunt. Illustrative 0.5 A excess current admits a strict nominal-resistance interval of 5.789474–9.619048 ohm; 1 A admits none. The fixed 8.2 ohm illustration bounds fully-on sink/current and instantaneous losses only. Actual source/receiver limits remain unavailable. No part or native circuit is selected, candidate/live electrical and copper deltas are zero, and protection/hardware qualification remains open.

SENSE-01 verifies captured sensing topology and manufacturer-limit discrepancies, with conditional divider arithmetic. Sensing and exact capacitor identities remain unqualified; the proposed correction has not been applied.
captured_findings: U1 PA2/pad 16 senses post-protection-diode VIN_RAW through 47 kΩ/6.8 kΩ, not battery-terminal voltage.
U1 PA4/pad 20 receives U8 INA180A1 converter-input branch current through a 20 mΩ shunt at gain 20. BEC_ONLY bypasses the shunt; whole-vehicle current is not measured.
C37's direct nominal 100 nF output load is 100 times the INA180 datasheet's listed 1 nF typical capacitive-load capability. Stability remains unqualified and actual oscillation is unmeasured.

The recorded R33 0.02R/1 W annotation conflicts with the exact Bourns CRA2512-FZ-R020ELF manufacturer rating of 3 W at 70 °C. Identity/annotation consistency is unresolved; no thermal uprating follows.
The exact C36/C37 KGM15ACG1H104KT orderable combination remains unverified; nominal 100 nF RC calculations do not validate the actual capacitor identity.
Actual V2 Stage A firmware has no ADC implementation.

conditional_results.qualification: Unqualified: minimum VDDA, transient and calibration envelopes remain unknown.

validated_results.proposed_next_change: Qualify exact C36/C37 and U8 filter/bypass parts and values, then apply an isolated output-loading correction and consistent R33 rating annotation. Preserve all candidates and sources; review divider/off-state and current-sense common-mode boundaries separately afterward.
validated_results.preservation: No circuit, native candidate or hardware change. VSERVO-01 electrical, POWER-DOC-01 presentation, both converters, exclusive source populations, 6S and disabled missing qualifications remain preserved.

validated_results.claim: SENSE-02 captured native verification passes the declared isolated sensing-filter delta: one old pin move and four added pins, exact TDK C36/C37 and C59 identities, Yageo R44 output isolation and consistent R33 annotation. All 27 mutation tests pass. These local captured-file and rejection checks do not establish physical qualification; effective capacitance, stability, ADC acquisition, off-state behavior and land/stencil approval remain held.
validated_results.preservation: Captured verification preserves 37 other source files, both converters and ACT-01 population bytes. C11 lands, separate IMU2, 6S and disabled missing qualifications are retained. Live CAD, copper, BOM and firmware remain unchanged; no hardware acceptance.

current_native_findings.scope_note: Strict gate retains the existing V2 ERC warning and detects the intentional PCB ground correction against the older preservation baseline; six component-limit blockers remain.

roadmap: Review divider scaling and power-off protection using established source/transient and minimum VDDA envelopes before choosing values or making range guarantees. Keep U8 filter stability, effective bypass capacitance, ADC acquisition and off-state behavior held; preserve 6S, both converters and exclusive source populations. Current-sense common mode remains open; shunt selection awaits the actual receiver/source envelope.
Qualify supply sequencing, C11/VSERVO transients, full 6S feed, leakage/damping, ADC and combined IMU2 before PCB integration.
Extend the implemented Stage A diagnostic after electrical acceptance; freeze the operational protocol and measure supervised-output failsafe behavior.
Complete V2 connector atlas, exact-part qualification, purchasing decisions and recorded board bring-up.
Measure voice quality, airtime and RC coexistence before selecting handheld radio, codec or hardware.
claim_boundaries: No verified range, autonomous navigation, speech quality or voice/RC coexistence result is claimed.
V1 source contains radio, GPS and PWM implementations but retains known safety and parsing defects.

A successful compile does not establish original deployed firmware, hardware operation or safety qualification.
PCB renders are CAD illustrations, not photographs of tested hardware.
Candidate purchasing CSVs are partial review lists, not complete approved orders or fabrication releases.
Handset source is absent; the multifunction handheld is proposed.
